paragraphs.text: Elders and sisters, all right, hope you had a great day today. It's been a busy day for us and I'm just now getting to the podcast, and this is going to be the conclusion of that chapter that we started last night relative to overcoming trials, and maybe the most important way to describe this is preparing yourselves to have trials of your faith whenever you set big goals or what we sometimes refer to as desires of the heart or righteous desires. The message to us is that the Lord is going to, he's going to test us and he's going to make sure that we really want these things and he's also going to want us to be prepared to be the kind of people that deserve his help.

Before I jump into this chapter though, I want to give the good news that some of you have probably already heard and that is that President Duterte has announced that the Metro Manila area is going to be going to general community quarantine or GCQ from what it was, which was modified ECQ, and that should give us a lot more flexibility going forward. We'll see in the next few days starting Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, we're going to watch real carefully and see what GCQ actually means in practical terms, and then we'll see what's going to happen as far as maybe transfers in the future and things like that. I wanted to give you that quick update.

All right, let's talk about some people who in the scriptures and in the early days of church experienced these trials of their faith and how they handled them and what we can learn from their experiences. Probably one of the best experiences that we can use as an example is in the book of Alma and involves the missionary labors of the sons of Mosiah. As you'll recall the story, these men were responsible for a very large population of the Lamanites becoming members of the church, and not just members but extraordinarily valiant members. These are the people who dug holes and threw their weapons and were prepared to die instead of giving up their covenants. These people were converted in the deepest sense of that word but it's interesting to note that these conversions did not happen easily or quickly.

This is from Alma 17 verses 5, 9, and 11: "For they," talking about the sons of Mosiah and their colleagues who also were their companions who went out to work with them, "for they had many afflictions; they did suffer much, both in body and in mind, such as hunger, thirst, and fatigue, and also much labor in the spirit." And they fasted much and prayed much that the Lord would grant unto them a portion of His Spirit to go with them and abide with them, that they might be an instrument in the hands of God to bring, if it were possible, their brethren, the Lamanites, to the knowledge of the truth. "And the Lord said unto them: Go forth among the Lamanites, your brethren, and establish my word; yet ye shall be patient in long-suffering and afflictions, that ye may show forth good examples unto them in me, and I will make an instrument of thee in my hands unto the salvation of many souls."

And so as we see this instruction from the Lord, we see a couple of very important points. Number one, He's saying, you've got to be patient in long-suffering and affliction so you can be good examples, but also so that you can prepare yourselves to be an instrument so that my Spirit can be with you. And it was, in fact, the Spirit that created the conversion. It wasn't the sons of Mosiah and their companions that created the conversion, it was the Spirit of the Lord that accompanied them that created the conversion.

Now this following quotation is sort of an excellent encapsulation of the whole experience. And I think you'll find it interesting because of the contrasts. And this is the account of Ammon and his brethren: "their journeyings in the land of Nephi, their sufferings in the land, their sorrows, and their afflictions, and their incomprehensible joy." That's Alma 28, verse 8. So in other words, even though they suffered much, they ultimately experienced great joy and satisfaction in their labors because they endured their trials of faith. We can suppose, elders and sisters, that had they not had any trials of faith, they wouldn't have had the same level of incomprehensible joy. Things that we obtain too easily, we really don't appreciate very much. The Lord understands this, of course, better than anyone. And so there's a very, very accurate price put on the blessings that come from heaven.

One of the most successful missionaries in the latter days is Wilford Woodruff. And I have a special connection to Wilford Woodruff because my great-great-grandfather, Zera Pulsipher, actually tracked it out, taught the gospel to, and baptized Wilford Woodruff. And so I'm kind of excited about that. Wilford Woodruff went on to be one of the great missionaries in the whole history of the gospel of Jesus Christ. So many people can trace their beginnings in the church or the beginnings of their ancestors in the church to Wilford Woodruff. But the story of Wilford Woodruff is a story not of success in the beginning, but of great affliction and failure for months and months and months. I think it was five months in his mission before he ever had a baptism. And that was very unusual in those days in the church.

Here's a little excerpt from his journal: "We cared not to go to the houses and get food, so we picked and ate raw corn and slept on the ground. We had walked all day one day without anything to eat and were very hungry and tired. But the minister, nor his wife, would give us anything to eat. They wouldn't let us stay overnight because we were Mormons. And the only chance we had was to go 12 miles farther down the river to an Indian trading post. And the wicked priest gave us the wrong directions and lied to us about the road and sent us through a swamp. And we had to wallow knee-deep in mud and water until 10 o'clock at night, just trying to follow the Crooked River. We then left the swamp and put out into the prairie and lay in the grass for the rest of the night." Just a quick little excerpt out of this great prophet who at the time was just a young missionary like yourselves and his missionary stories.

It's interesting that he had not just that affliction, but his companion, after these early afflictions occurred, just quit and went home. He just got up one day and said, "Wilford, I'm done." And he took off and went back to Utah and left Wilford Woodruff by himself for quite a long time in the mission field. But it was at that time when Wilford did not quit, that success started to come his way. So as you look at opposition, as you look at your own trials of your faith, first of all, recognize that they are a trial of faith. It's not about you being some bad person. That's not what it's about. It's the Lord testing you, trying you, sanctifying you, purifying you—embrace it, don't resist it, don't be someone who whines and complains about it, because then you won't gain from it.

Reflect on this statement from President Spencer W. Kimball: "I have on occasion cited the need for many reservoirs in our lives to provide for our needs. I have said some reservoirs are to store water. Some are to store food, as we do in our family welfare program, and as Joseph did in the land of Egypt during the seven years of plenty. There should also be reservoirs of knowledge to meet the future needs, reservoirs of courage to overcome the floods of fear that put uncertainty in our lives, reservoirs of physical strength to help us meet the frequent burdens of work and illness. Reservoirs of goodness, reservoirs of stamina, reservoirs of faith—yes, especially reservoirs of faith, so that when the world presses in upon us, we can stand firm and strong. When the temptations of a decaying," and I should add increasingly permissive and wicked world about us, "draw on our energies and sap our vitality and seek to pull us down, we need to have a storage of faith that can carry us forward over these difficult times and terrifying moments and disappointments, years of adversity. If we have these reservoirs of faith, we can endure it well."

The second thing in enduring your trials of faith is to read and reflect upon the following scriptures. This one from Alma 36, verse 3: "I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions." And this one from Matthew chapter 11, verses 28 to 30: "Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light."

Number three, when you feel a need for a spiritual lift in times of disappointment or discouragement, read and reread Alma chapter 17 through 26. If you will read these chapters prayerfully, you'll be inspired and given strength to endure your trials of faith. Number four, memorize the phrase: "for after much tribulation come the blessings." That is a verse in the Doctrine and Covenants, section 58, verse 4. Number five, identify a personal collection of favorite scriptures and quotations and read them when your faith is being tried.

I might add, I do this every day, and I've done this every day for many years. I have 24 cards that I review on a daily basis that give me powerful quotations, scriptures, quotes from the prophets, modern and ancient, and other wise people that help me see things more clearly when things are going badly. So not just in a bad time, but in all times. Build your own reservoir of powerful quotations and powerful scriptures that are available to you and review them every day, not just in the bad days. Just as you review them every day, you will have fewer bad days.

Now I want to give you a caution, no matter who you are. And even if you are consistently prayerful in the process of selecting righteous desires, there will be times when you'll begin to exercise faith and a desire that is not approved by your Father in heaven. When this is the case, you'll experience a stupor of thought and will find it virtually impossible to focus your mind on your desires. When this happens, you should cease your effort to exercise faith regarding that desire and make every effort to prayerfully determine why the desire is not appropriate.

In your effort to exercise faith, it is your responsibility to ensure that you do not confuse either your lack of personal worthiness or desire or personal discipline or a trial of faith with that stupor of thought. They are very distinctly different experiences. When you're not worthy, you know it. When you're not exercising personal discipline, you know it. When you're going through a trial of faith, you know it. And when there's a stupor of thought, if you'll think about it deeply, you will know it. If you're sensitive to the Spirit, you'll be able to discern very clearly between a trial of faith and a stupor of thought, which occurs only when a desire, for one reason or another, is not what the Lord wants you working on right now.

With this understanding, elders and sisters, you should be able to consistently have the assurance that your desires are righteous and approved of the Lord. You should keep this caution in mind because through persistence it is possible to obtain goals and desires that in the wisdom of the Lord are not in your best interest. The Lord will honor our agency in the desires we seek. If we push really hard on something that we know we shouldn't, we might just get it and then we will regret we have it. And I think that's a great caution to keep in mind.

So in conclusion, let's just go through the 17 key steps to obtaining power from heaven. Number one, a clear understanding of faith as a principle of power. Number two, a realization that the powers of heaven are governed by our individual faith. Number three, living righteously. Number four, prayerfully selecting righteous goals. Five, specifying your goals in writing. Six, specify when your goals will be attained. That means putting a timeline on your goal, not just open-ended. Number seven, plead your case before the Lord, telling him what effort or sacrifice you are willing to make to achieve your goal.

Number eight, consistently think about your goal. Number nine, use all of your willpower to think positively about your potential to achieve your goal with the Lord's help. Number 10, consistently remind yourself that the added power and strength from God that is at your disposal is based on your individual faith. Number 11, remember the Lord is anxious to grant your righteous desires if you will but qualify yourself. 12, make your specific goal a matter of constant prayer. 13, pray that the Lord will enhance your ability, strengthen your intellect, strengthen your stamina and capacity, and also expand in exercising your faith as a principle of power. It is a gift from God that you should be praying for.

Number 14, when you face a situation that causes you to doubt your ability to achieve your goal, learn to offer a mental prayer immediately to request the Lord's help. Then exercise faith that he will help you, remembering that if you lack faith, you deny the Lord the opportunity to assist you. Number 15, repeatedly reflect on the promise made by the Savior: "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you." That's Matthew 7, verse 7. 16, recognize at the outset that your faith most likely will be tried. Go into any major goal where you're seeking to draw down the powers of heaven, knowing full well that you will have to go through the fire to get it. And it's okay because the fire will purify you. You will come out of the fire and you will be more valuable even than the goal you're seeking because of what you became in the pursuit of that goal. And then number 17, make certain you do your part in the effort to achieve your righteous desires. It's not enough just to pray and to exercise faith in heaven giving you power. You have to go out and take action as well.

Elders and sisters, it's been great going through this with you. I hope you found it valuable. I'm going to try to buy enough of these books and have them shipped so I can give each one of you one of these books. I don't know that I'll pull it off, but it's my goal and I'm going for it. So I'm going to try to get them and if I can't get them in time before we leave the mission, then I'll keep trying to get them and I'll get them sent out to you. Anyway, I love you very much. Hope you're doing well tonight and we'll talk to you tomorrow.
